items.name: tools.list
items.since: Introduced anna-app-runtime v0.1 · current v0.15.0 / dispatcher 0.19.0
items.summary: Return every Executa `tool_id` this window is *currently allowed* to invoke. Pure ACL projection — no Agent round-trip, no NATS call. Useful at bundle boot to decide which UI buttons to render before the user clicks.

wire.auth: Handled by the host page — the bundle never sees the token. Transport details (`POST /api/v1/anna-apps/runtime/rpc`, `X-Anna-App-Token`, envelope wrapping) are described once in the section overview.

items.signature: anna.tools.list(args?: {}, opts?: {timeoutMs?: number}) => Promise<{tools: Array<{tool_id: string, status?: 'available'|'deploying'|'unavailable'}>}>

returns.type: { tools: Array<{ tool_id: string, status?: string }> }
returns.desc:
Flat array of `{tool_id}` objects. Order is `required_executas` first, then `optional_executas`, both filtered through `_is_tool_allowed`.

**Inclusion rule.** A tool appears iff *both* hold:
• It is declared in `manifest.required_executas[].tool_id` *or* `manifest.optional_executas[].tool_id`.
• It is matched by an entry in `manifest.ui.host_api.tools` — either `"required:*"` (all required), `"optional:*"` (all optional), the bare `tool_id`, or any prefixed form whose suffix after the final `:` equals `<tool_id>` (the runtime gate `_is_tool_allowed` does a `:<tool_id>` suffix match). NOTE: the runtime accepts any such prefix, but the CLI `anna-app validate` (`@anna-ai/app-schema`) only permits the canonical authoring forms — `required:*`, `optional:*`, `required:<id>`, `optional:<id>`, a bare `<id>`, or `bundled:<handle>` — so write your manifest using those.

This call ignores user-grant state and runtime availability: a `tool_id` may be listed even if the Executa Agent for the user is offline. To know whether a tool will *actually run*, you must call `tools.invoke` and handle `agent_unavailable`.

**`status` (optional; dispatcher ≥ 0.14.0).** When the host implements the `get_tool_availability` store hook, each entry carries `status: 'available' | 'deploying' | 'unavailable'` computed from the deploy-reconciliation facts table — use it to disable buttons before a click fails with `executa_not_deployed`. Hosts/harnesses without the hook return the legacy shape (no `status`); treat a missing field as unknown, not available.

errors.name: permission_denied
errors.desc: Window token does not authorise this namespace. Usually means the bundle was loaded into a window whose manifest revision no longer matches.

errors.name: invalid_token
errors.desc: `X-Anna-App-Token` is missing, expired, or signed for a different `window_uuid`.

limitations: Result is a snapshot — subscribe with `anna.tools.onChanged(cb)` (SDK ≥ 0.12.0; fires on the `tools.changed` window event after deploy reconciliation lands tools on the agent) and re-run `tools.list()` instead of polling. Manifest-revision changes still require a window reload.
Does not call into the Executa Agent. A `tool_id` in the list can still fail at invoke time with `agent_unavailable` if no Agent is online for the user.
No paging: a manifest with 1000+ tools returns them all in one response. Manifest schema currently caps `required + optional` at 64 entries, so this is not a practical issue.

items.name: tools.invoke
items.since: Introduced anna-app-runtime v0.1 · timeoutMs since v0.3 · current v0.15.0 / dispatcher 0.19.0
items.direction: Bundle (iframe) → Host RPC → Executa Agent (NATS) → plugin
items.summary: Invoke a single Executa tool *directly from the bundle*, bypassing the LLM. The host enforces the `host_api.tools` whitelist, mints credentials, negotiates a deadline, calls the user's online Executa Agent over NATS, and returns the plugin's payload — two envelope layers stripped — to the iframe.

wire.auth: Handled by the host page — the bundle never sees the token. Transport details (`POST /api/v1/anna-apps/runtime/rpc`, `X-Anna-App-Token`, envelope wrapping) are described once in the section overview.
wire.upstream_nats: executa.invoke_tool — params={plugin_name, tool_name, arguments, timeout?, deadline_ms?, credentials?} (relevant when debugging the Agent leg)

items.signature: anna.tools.invoke(args: {tool_id: string, method?: string, args?: object, timeoutMs?: number}, opts?: {timeoutMs?: number}) => Promise<object>

params.name: tool_id
params.summary: Server-minted Executa tool id; must be present in the `tools.list` projection.
notes: Format is opaque. Mint-only ids look like `tool-{handle}-{slug}-{uniq}` (no separator); legacy ids use `plugin.tool` or `plugin__tool` — both still routed by `_split_tool_id`.

Must match an entry in `manifest.ui.host_api.tools`. The runtime gate `_is_tool_allowed` accepts `required:*`, `optional:*`, the bare id, or any ref ending in `:<tool_id>`; otherwise `permission_denied`. For authoring, the CLI `anna-app validate` only permits the canonical forms `required:*` / `optional:*` / `required:<id>` / `optional:<id>` / bare `<id>` / `bundled:<handle>`.
Reject reasons (HostRpcError `invalid_arg`): missing, empty, or non-string.

params.name: method
params.summary: Plugin-side method name. **Required** for mint-only `tool_id`s that contain no `.` or `__` separator.
notes: When omitted, the host falls back to splitting `tool_id` on the first `__` or `.` separator — failing with `invalid_arg` if neither is present.
When provided, `tool_id` is used verbatim as `plugin_name` and `method` becomes `tool_name` on the NATS call.
Must be a string when set; non-string types raise `invalid_arg`.

params.name: args
params.summary: Structured tool arguments forwarded verbatim to the plugin as `arguments`.
notes: JSON-serialised by the SDK; functions, BigInts, and cyclic refs are rejected at `postMessage` time.
Schema is plugin-defined — see the Executa's manifest `tools[].parameters`. The host does not validate field-level shape; an unknown field is silently passed through (or rejected by the plugin).

params.name: timeoutMs
params.summary: Caller-requested plugin-facing deadline in **milliseconds**. Clamped server-side to `[ANNA_APP_TOOLS_INVOKE_TIMEOUT_MIN_MS, _MAX_MS]` (defaults 1 000 / **90 000** — the public edge's held-request ceiling, forum #199). Calls that need more must use `tools.invokeAsync`.
notes: Booleans are rejected explicitly (`invalid_arg`) — `True`/`False` would otherwise clamp via the `bool ⊂ int` quirk.
When omitted, the Agent falls back to the per-tool `timeout` declared in the Executa manifest, or `ANNA_APP_TOOLS_INVOKE_TIMEOUT_DEFAULT_MS` (65 000) if neither side declares one.
Host wall-clock wait = clamped value + `ANNA_APP_TOOLS_INVOKE_TIMEOUT_GRACE_MS` (2 000) so an in-flight ack/cancel has room to land before `tool_timeout` fires.
SDK default per-call timeout is 70 000 ms (`DEFAULT_TIMEOUTS_BY_NS.tools`); pass a larger value here *and* in `opts.timeoutMs` if the plugin needs longer.
Clamp-down is observable: when a clamped call later times out, `error.details` carries `requested_timeout_ms` / `max_timeout_ms` alongside the effective `timeout_ms`.

returns.desc:
The plugin's `invoke` payload, with both envelope layers stripped.

The raw NATS reply is `{success: bool, data: {success: bool, tool, data: <payload>, error?}}` (see *executa-invoke-result-shape*). The host:
1. On a failed **outer** envelope, first classifies plugin JSON-RPC errors (structured `data.jsonrpc_error.code` from Agent ≥ 1.1.0-beta.33, else the `"invoke error: {'code': ..."` string): `-32602` → `invalid_arg`, `-32601`/`-32603`/`-32000..-32099` → `tool_failed` (both carry `details.jsonrpc_code` + `source: "plugin"`); anything else → `executa_unavailable`.
2. Rejects with `tool_failed` if the **inner** envelope is missing or `success != true`.
3. Returns `invoke.data` if it's an object, else `{}`.

Most plugins return a domain payload (e.g. `{state, etag}`); callers should treat unknown keys as additive.

errors.name: invalid_arg
errors.desc: `tool_id` missing/empty/non-string, `method` non-string, `timeoutMs` non-int (or bool), or `tool_id` carries no separator AND no `method` was supplied. ALSO: the plugin itself rejected the arguments (raised → JSON-RPC `-32602`); then `details` carries `{jsonrpc_code: -32602, source: "plugin"}` — do not retry, fix the args.

errors.name: permission_denied
errors.desc: `tool_id` is not whitelisted by `manifest.ui.host_api.tools` for this window.

errors.name: agent_unavailable
errors.desc: No Executa Agent is currently online for the calling user (checked via `agent_presence_service`).

errors.name: tool_timeout
errors.desc: Host wall-clock wait (`timeoutMs + grace_ms`) elapsed before the Agent acked. `details` carries `{tool_id, timeout_ms}` and any deadline metadata the Agent attached.

errors.name: executa_unavailable
errors.desc: Outer NATS envelope reported `success != true` for transport-level reasons (Agent crashed, NATS rejection, stdio protocol breakage `-32700`/`-32600`). Plugin application errors (`-32602`, `-32601`, `-32603`, `-32000..-32099`) no longer land here — they classify to `invalid_arg` / `tool_failed`.

errors.name: tool_failed
errors.desc: Plugin executed but reported failure — via `success: false` envelope (or a non-dict), OR via raise → JSON-RPC `-32601`/`-32603`/`-32000..-32099` (then `details` carries `{jsonrpc_code, source: "plugin"}`). The plugin's error string is surfaced verbatim in `message`.

errors.name: not_implemented
errors.desc: Store does not support `invoke_executa_tool` (local-dev harness without a NATS bridge).

errors.name: not_found
errors.desc: Resolved `user_id` no longer exists (token validated but row deleted between auth and dispatch).

limitations: Synchronous ceiling is **90 s** (edge-bound). Work that may exceed it must go through the async job channel — `tools.invokeAsync` / `getJob` / `cancelJob` / `listJobs` (dispatcher ≥ 0.19.0).
Per-call `timeoutMs` is **silently clamped** to policy bounds — out-of-range values do not raise. Read back the host's `details.timeout_ms` on `tool_timeout` to see what was actually used.

Manifest-side per-tool overrides are not yet threaded through the host store; today only the caller value and the policy default apply. The Agent honours its own manifest `tool_def.timeout` when the caller omits `timeoutMs`.
Routing picks the user's `default_agent_client_id` when online, otherwise the first online Agent — there is no client_id pinning from the bundle side.

Credentials (`PlatformCredentialService.resolve_all_plugin_credentials`) are best-effort: a failure resolves to `None` and the plugin runs without credentials. Plugins must handle missing-credential cases.
The plugin payload (`invoke.data`) is forced to an object — non-dict returns surface as `{}`. Plugins that need to return scalars or arrays must wrap them (e.g. `{value: ...}`).

items.name: tools.invokeAsync
items.direction: Bundle (iframe) → Host RPC (instant) → job row + NATS long command → Executa Agent → plugin
items.summary: Start a long-running tool call as a host-owned **job** and return immediately with a `jobId`. No held-open HTTP request anywhere in the chain — this is the only correct channel for tools that may exceed the 90 s synchronous ceiling. Execution state lives in the host DB; updates arrive via `tool_job` window events (push) and `tools.getJob` (authoritative pull).

wire.auth: Handled by the host page — the bundle never sees the token. Transport details (`POST /api/v1/anna-apps/runtime/rpc`, `X-Anna-App-Token`, envelope wrapping) are described once in the section overview.
wire.upstream_nats: rpc.executa / invoke_tool as a long-running command (command_id == jobId == plugin invoke_id, `tjob_<hex32>`); progress rides matrix.progress.{client_id}.{jobId}

items.signature: anna.tools.invokeAsync(args: {tool_id: string, method?: string, args?: object, timeoutMs?: number, clientTag?: string}) => Promise<{jobId: string, state: "queued", deadlineMs: number}>

params.name: tool_id
params.summary: Server-minted Executa tool id; same whitelist gate (`host_api.tools`) as `tools.invoke`.
notes: Mint-only ids (`tool-{handle}-{slug}-{uniq}`) carry no separator — pass the plugin method via `method`.

params.name: method
params.summary: Plugin-side method name; **required** for mint-only `tool_id`s (same splitting rules as `tools.invoke`).

params.name: args
params.summary: Structured tool arguments, forwarded verbatim to the plugin. Size cap 64 KB (`invalid_arg` beyond).

params.name: timeoutMs
params.summary: The **job deadline** — how long the plugin may run. Clamped to [60 000, 86 400 000] (60 s – 24 h). Unlike the sync channel this is not edge-bound: no HTTP request is held open.
notes: Deadline elapsed without a terminal state → job flips to `expired` with error `tool_timeout`, and the host sends the agent a cancel.
Values below 60 s are raised to 60 s — calls that fit under 90 s should use plain `tools.invoke` instead.

params.name: clientTag
params.summary: Caller-defined correlation tag (≤120 chars), stored on the job row and filterable in `tools.listJobs` — the key to re-adopting jobs after an iframe reload.

returns.desc: `{jobId, state: "queued", deadlineMs}`. `jobId` matches `^tjob_[0-9a-f]{32}$` and equals the plugin-side `invoke_id` (one id across app, host, agent, audit). `deadlineMs` is an absolute epoch-milliseconds wall clock.

errors.name: permission_denied
errors.desc: `tool_id` not whitelisted by `manifest.ui.host_api.tools`.

errors.name: invalid_arg
errors.desc: Bad `tool_id`/`method`/`timeoutMs`/`clientTag` types, `args` not an object or > 64 KB.

errors.name: job_quota_exceeded
errors.desc: The user already has 5 active (queued/running) jobs. `details` carries `{max_active, active}`.

errors.name: agent_unavailable
errors.desc: No online agent and wake failed; also returned (with an upgrade hint) when the agent predates the job-capable version.

errors.name: agent_waking
errors.desc: Cloud Agent is resuming — retry after `details.retry_after_ms` (the SDK's `invokeAsyncAwait` does not auto-retry creation; surface a spinner).

errors.name: not_implemented
errors.desc: Host predates dispatcher 0.19.0 or the async channel is disabled.

limitations: Per-user active job quota: 5. Per-agent long-job concurrency: 3 — excess jobs fail fast with `long_job_capacity` (fold into the job's error; retryable).
Result cap 256 KB — larger payloads must be stored via `host/uploadFile` and returned as a reference (`result_too_large` otherwise).
The `tool_job` push events never carry the result; always `getJob` after a terminal event.
Terminal jobs are retained 30 days, then purged (progress cascades).

items.name: tools.getJob
items.direction: Bundle (iframe) → Host RPC → job row read (no Agent round-trip)
items.summary: Authoritative snapshot of one job + an incremental progress slice. This is the single source of truth: `tool_job` push events are a latency optimisation and may be dropped — `getJob` never lies. Also the reload-recovery read and the polling fallback used by `invokeAsyncAwait`.

wire.auth: Handled by the host page — the bundle never sees the token. Transport details (`POST /api/v1/anna-apps/runtime/rpc`, `X-Anna-App-Token`, envelope wrapping) are described once in the section overview.

items.signature: anna.tools.getJob(args: {jobId: string, sinceSeq?: number, limit?: number}) => Promise<JobSnapshot>

params.name: sinceSeq
params.summary: Return only progress events with `seq > sinceSeq`. Feed back the previous response's `lastSeq` for cheap incremental reads.

params.name: limit
params.summary: Max progress events in the slice (1–500).

returns.desc: `JobSnapshot`: `{jobId, toolId, state, createdAt, updatedAt, deadlineMs (epoch ms), clientTag?, result? (succeeded only), error? ({code, message, details?}; failed/cancelled/expired only), progress: [{seq, ts, type, data}], lastSeq, lastHeartbeatAt}`. `state` ∈ queued | running | succeeded | failed | cancelled | expired.

errors.name: job_not_found
errors.desc: `jobId` does not exist **or belongs to another user** — ownership misses are indistinguishable from absence by design (no existence oracle).

errors.name: invalid_arg
errors.desc: `jobId` not matching `^tjob_[0-9a-f]{32}$`, out-of-range `sinceSeq`/`limit`, over-long `clientTag`/`reason`, or bad `state`/`since` values.

errors.name: not_implemented
errors.desc: Host predates dispatcher 0.19.0, or the async channel is disabled (`ANNA_APP_TOOLS_ASYNC_ENABLED=false`).

limitations: Progress is a per-job ring of the **latest 500** events — a slow reader can miss early events (the terminal state + result are never in the ring, they're on the row).
Progress event `data` is truncated to 8 KB per event (`{_truncated: true}` placeholder beyond).

items.name: tools.cancelJob
items.direction: Bundle (iframe) → Host RPC → job transition + `_cancel_invoke` fast-path command → Agent
items.summary: Cooperative, idempotent cancel. Active job: the row flips to `cancelled` immediately (user-visible), then the agent gracefully cancels the command task — the plugin process and its other concurrent invokes are untouched; a process-group kill is only the 500 ms fallback for a truly stuck task. Terminal job: `{cancelled: false}` no-op.

wire.auth: Handled by the host page — the bundle never sees the token. Transport details (`POST /api/v1/anna-apps/runtime/rpc`, `X-Anna-App-Token`, envelope wrapping) are described once in the section overview.
wire.upstream_nats: _cancel_invoke fast-path on matrix.command.{client_id} with {job_id, plugin_name, tool_name, reason}

items.signature: anna.tools.cancelJob(args: {jobId: string, reason?: string}) => Promise<{jobId: string, state: JobState, cancelled: boolean}>

params.name: reason
params.summary: Free-text audit note (≤200 chars); lands in the job's error message.

returns.desc: `{jobId, state, cancelled}`. `cancelled: true` iff this call performed the transition; repeating the call (or cancelling a finished job) returns the terminal `state` with `cancelled: false`.

errors.name: job_not_found
errors.desc: `jobId` does not exist **or belongs to another user** — ownership misses are indistinguishable from absence by design (no existence oracle).

errors.name: invalid_arg
errors.desc: `jobId` not matching `^tjob_[0-9a-f]{32}$`, out-of-range `sinceSeq`/`limit`, over-long `clientTag`/`reason`, or bad `state`/`since` values.

errors.name: not_implemented
errors.desc: Host predates dispatcher 0.19.0, or the async channel is disabled (`ANNA_APP_TOOLS_ASYNC_ENABLED=false`).

limitations: Cancel is cooperative — a plugin in a tight uninterruptible loop is only stopped by the 500 ms process-group-kill fallback, which reaps the WHOLE plugin process (other in-flight invokes of the same plugin included).
A `succeeded` result racing the cancel is absorbed idempotently: the row stays `cancelled`, the late result is kept for audit only.

items.name: tools.listJobs
items.direction: Bundle (iframe) → Host RPC → job rows read (no Agent round-trip)
items.summary: Enumerate the current user's recent jobs — the reload-recovery entry point. After an iframe reload (or in a second window) call `listJobs({clientTag, state: ["queued","running"]})` to find in-flight work, then drive each job with `getJob({sinceSeq})`.

wire.auth: Handled by the host page — the bundle never sees the token. Transport details (`POST /api/v1/anna-apps/runtime/rpc`, `X-Anna-App-Token`, envelope wrapping) are described once in the section overview.

items.signature: anna.tools.listJobs(args?: {tool_id?: string, state?: JobState | JobState[], clientTag?: string, since?: string, limit?: number}) => Promise<{jobs: JobSnapshot[], truncated: boolean}>

params.name: state
params.summary: One or more of queued | running | succeeded | failed | cancelled | expired.

params.name: clientTag
params.summary: Exact match on the tag passed at `invokeAsync` time — scope recovery to YOUR batch.

params.name: since
params.summary: RFC3339 lower bound on `createdAt`; lookback capped at 7 days.

returns.desc: `{jobs: JobSnapshot[], truncated}` — snapshots carry an EMPTY `progress` slice (fetch per-job history via `getJob`); `truncated: true` means more rows matched than `limit`.

errors.name: invalid_arg
errors.desc: `jobId` not matching `^tjob_[0-9a-f]{32}$`, out-of-range `sinceSeq`/`limit`, over-long `clientTag`/`reason`, or bad `state`/`since` values.

errors.name: not_implemented
errors.desc: Host predates dispatcher 0.19.0, or the async channel is disabled (`ANNA_APP_TOOLS_ASYNC_ENABLED=false`).

limitations: Terminal jobs age out after 30 days (retention purge).
Snapshots in the list carry no progress events — one `getJob` per adopted job.
